title: Kummer tower solving degree at a prime with v2(p - 1) = 40 and at the NIST P-224 prime
status_note: Blocked on the generic-field F4 lane (in progress, not yet pushed): today's tower engine works over primes below 2^32, so every recorded Kummer D is at p1 = 15*2^27 + 1 or similar. The argv below uses pkm_tower_pilot's current flags; the generic-field lane may rename them, and PROTOCOL.md fixes the final command.
blocked_on: branch:claude/f4-generic-field generic-field F4 lane, in progress (not yet pushed); needs the tower engine over a 45-bit and a 224-bit prime

notes: research/pkm_dickson_torus_20261015/README.md on branch claude/leads-dickson-torus (recorded Kummer D at p1: m = 2, N = 2..20; m = 3, N <= 15; m = 4, N <= 12)

question: Is the Kummer tower's F4 solving degree D at fixed (m, N) the same at a 45-bit prime with v2(p - 1) = 40 and at the P-224 prime as at the 31-bit p1 where every recorded value was measured?
decision_value: Every PKM solving-degree number in the repository is measured over a prime below 2^32; whether it transfers to the field of the curve it is about has never been checked. If D at p = 27*2^40 + 1 and at the P-224 prime equals the p1 value in every cell, lead 1's answer (from the cheaper p1 runs) speaks for P-224 and the small-prime ladder stays the instrument; if D differs in any cell, every p1 extrapolation in the encyclopedia is suspect and lead 1 has to be rerun at the real field. Depths beyond 27 tower levels exist only at these primes, so this card is also the first place a deeper Kummer tower can be built at all.

resources.notes: Cost = (recorded p1 cost of the same cell) x F, F the multi-limb slowdown of the generic-field engine at 45 and 224 bits, which the generic-field lane measures. The p1 cells this card repeats are small (m = 3, N = 15: 1.1 GB, 6.0 min; m = 2, N <= 20 and m = 4, N <= 12 below that), so with F in the tens the whole card is hours to a few days of one core; memory grows with the limb count (x2 at 45 bits, x7 at 224 bits for 32-bit limbs).

outputs.result_schema: pkm_tower_pilot JSONL rows, compared cell by cell with the recorded p1 rows

cairn.notes: Two single runs, one per prime. Not preemptible until the engine checkpoints.

env.name: crypto-f4-generic
env.recipe: A rust:1.98 image built at the generic-field lane's merge commit with `cargo build --release --example pkm_tower_pilot --example pkm_tower_check`, imported with `cairn lab env import crypto-f4-generic-<sha> --docker <image>`

funding.rationale: Second: cheap once the engine exists, and it decides whether every small-prime solving degree (lead 1 included) speaks for the P-224 field at all.
